design_notes: Lead each section with a plain-language explanation before any number or citation. Avoid 'delve', 'robust', 'seamless'. Use concrete examples (e.g., 'Western Railway has been a client since 2006'). The intro must orient a reader who knows nothing about the company. Ensure every claim is grounded in source_ids from the DRHP pages.

The financials section will be heavy on numbers; use a table to convey trends clearly. The valuation section needs a small table for EPS/NAV/P/E; note that the P/E using issue price is not yet calculable. The offer section should clarify that the issue price is undetermined. For risks, pull the most striking ones: customer concentration (57%), negative cash flow, recent low-price share issuance. The governance section should note the 90.949% promoter holding and the struck-off companies.

beats.beat: The company operates in two segments: infrastructure creation (contracts for railways, bridges, roads) and operating a ready-mix concrete (RMC) plant at Thane, Maharashtra.

Contracts are won through a competitive bidding process: the client floats a tender, a pre-bid meeting is held, the lowest quote typically wins a Letter of Acceptance, and the contractor deposits a performance guarantee before work begins.

Major clients include Western Railways, Central Railways, Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation (MRVCL), Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM), Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA), Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation, and others. Western Railway has been a client since 2006 and contributed 52% of the order book as of the latest date.

The company highlights its long-standing relationships, expertise in box-pushing construction techniques, modern machinery, and a strong order book as competitive strengths. It is primarily active in Mumbai and consolidating its position across Maharashtra.
Revenue is heavily concentrated: the top few customers accounted for 57% of total revenue in fiscal 2018.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations has been on a declining trend: from ₹9,021.12 lakhs in fiscal 2015, it fell to ₹8,661.35 lakhs in 2016, then to ₹7,452.76 lakhs in 2017, ₹7,344.47 lakhs in 2018, and further to ₹6,053.05 lakhs for the ten-month period ended June 30, 2018 (note: the reporting period may vary).

Net profit after adjustments was volatile: it stood at ₹95.95 lakhs in fiscal 2015, dropped sharply to ₹78.36 lakhs in 2016, ₹32.63 lakhs in 2017, and a mere ₹15.86 lakhs in 2018, before surging to ₹314.66 lakhs for the ten-month period ended June 30, 2018. The large jump in the latest period is a key item to understand.
EBITDA also fluctuated: ₹784.46 lakhs (2015), ₹945.78 lakhs (2016), ₹783.31 lakhs (2017), ₹676.19 lakhs (2018), and ₹928.80 lakhs (ten months ended June 30, 2018).

Total assets grew from ₹7,062.34 lakhs (2014) to ₹8,232.15 lakhs (as of June 30, 2018). Long-term borrowings decreased significantly from ₹586.63 lakhs (2014) to ₹133.09 lakhs (2018), but short-term borrowings increased from ₹3,082.27 lakhs to ₹3,537.35 lakhs over the same period.
The company has reported negative cash flows in recent years, which is flagged as a risk. Failure to recover trade receivables on time could also affect financial condition.

Key accounting ratios computed by the company: EPS (face value ₹10) was ₹4.14 (FY2016), ₹1.97 (FY2017), and ₹28.14 (FY2018 for the ten-month period). P/E ratios based on the issue price (to be determined) are not yet calculable. NAV per share was ₹12.39 (basis 1), ₹44.71 (basis 2) – the basis difference is not disclosed in the excerpts.

beats.beat: The sole promoter is Amit Bholanath Mishra, who holds 74,95,476 equity shares – 90.949% of the pre-issue capital. Other directors hold only 300 shares each.
Key management personnel include Ms. Anchal Pachori (CFO, aged 28, CA) and Mr. Mohit Soni (Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, aged 26, ACS).

Related party transactions include loans taken from KMP/directors of ₹68.4 lakhs and director remuneration of ₹57.7 lakhs in fiscal 2018. Outstanding payables to related parties stood at ₹324.3 lakhs as of March 31, 2018.

No criminal cases or investigations have been filed against directors, and neither the promoter nor directors are on the RBI list of willful defaulters. However, two companies promoted by the promoter – Al-Noor Chickens Private Limited and A B Magma Automobiles Private Limited – were struck off by the ROC in March 2016 for non-operation.
The company has not appointed an independent agency to appraise the project, and there is no external monitoring agency for fund deployment.

beats.beat: The company operates in the Indian infrastructure and construction sector, which includes power, bridges, dams, roads, and urban infrastructure. The sector contributes about 8% to India’s GDP (at constant prices).

Demand is driven by government flagship programs such as the 100 Smart Cities Mission, Atal Mission for Urban Rejuvenation and Transformation (AMRUT), Make in India, and Power for All. Eased FDI norms in 15 sectors, rising urbanization, and population growth also support growth.

The logistics sector in India is expected to grow at a CAGR of 10.5%, from US$160 billion in 2017 to US$215 billion by 2020. Infrastructure spending as a percentage of GDP was 9.0% during the 12th Five-Year Plan (2012-2017).
The market is highly fragmented and working-capital-intensive, with competition from both organized and unorganized players.
Key headwinds include the slow pace of government projects, working capital crunches that can affect profitability, and changes in government policies.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild is a Mumbai-based infrastructure contractor that builds railways, bridges, roads and runs a ready-mix concrete plant. It primarily serves government clients such as Western Railways and the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai.
The company is raising up to 44.28 lakh equity shares via a fresh issue (no offer for sale) to fund working capital and general corporate purposes. The issue price is yet to be determined (₹[●]).
Almost 91% of its equity is held by promoter Amit Bholanath Mishra before the issue, and the company depends on a single customer – Indian Railways – for 57% of its revenue.

beats.beat: The issue is a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares of face value ₹10 each at an issue price to be determined (₹[●] per share). There is no offer for sale component.
The proceeds will be used primarily to meet working capital requirements of ₹1,130 lakhs, with the remainder allocated to general corporate purposes (amount to be determined).
The lead manager to the issue is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited and the registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited.

The company has not appointed any independent agency for project appraisal, and no monitoring agency has been appointed – fund deployment will be at the discretion of the management, monitored by the Audit Committee.

beats.beat: Customer concentration risk: Indian Railways (specifically Western Railway) is the largest customer, contributing 57% of revenue and 52% of the order book. Losing this client would severely impact revenue.
Order book risk: contracts may be adjusted, cancelled, or suspended by clients, so the order book is not a reliable indicator of future revenue.
Negative cash flow: the company has reported negative cash flows in recent years, which could adversely affect operations if sustained.
Liquidity risk: the company had unsecured loans of ₹405.02 lakhs as of March 31, 2018, repayable on demand. A sudden repayment demand could strain cash flow.
Regulatory and approval risks: the company requires numerous licenses and permits; failure to obtain or renew them could disrupt operations.
Litigation: pending legal proceedings against the company, promoter, and directors could result in liabilities and penalties.
Issue price risk: the issue price may not be indicative of the market price after listing, and the stock could trade below the issue price.
Recent share issuance: the company issued equity shares in the last 12 months at a price that may be lower than the issue price.
